message:
Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the parts connect end to end at the midspan antinode with nothing on the deck. In plain words bridge motion drives the two masses where motion is largest and the clamped frame carries the push into the girders. The chain is central twin-mass zone to spring-plus-damper zone to single short transverse cross-beam zone to left beam-end-to-girder-web clamp zone and right beam-end-to-girder-web clamp zone to left girder host zone and right girder host zone from the layout sketch (E55) and the transverse clamp sketch (E74), transverse perpendicular not longitudinal, with two masses and two spring sets and two dampers and one beam, High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), bolts only in the clamp zones, Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), axes diagonal, and zero items above the deck.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the numbers fit everyday feel and girder space with reconciled weight. In plain words bare shake is near body weight while damped shake is a small fraction and motion fits in a hand. Retrofitted 0.67 m/s2 from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) is 0.068 times gravity inside Medium 0.5 to 1.0 m/s2 versus bare 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 times gravity outside everyday feel, travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) clears 80 mm stops with sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) totalling 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68) inside girder depth, slip 32.9 kN per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) exceeds 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65) with 8.40 kN stop hit from the stop-force calculation (E66), about 42 body weights against about 16 body weights, and added Tuned Mass Damper weight 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) is 1.31 percent from the weight-fraction calculation (E72) of 600 kN live load from the live-load estimate (E30) while total with about 230 kg beam steel at 2.26 kN is 1.69 percent from the total-weight calculation (E76) inside the 2 percent rule, where 0.133 percent from the added-weight check (E71) is kilograms over newtons and is dropped.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, there are no open blocking objections and all four readiness opinions on proposal v1 are answered as ready. In plain words tuning, clamp, from-below service and Medium comfort all close in this version, and the drawing failure from the inspiration record (A1) says nothing about the design because transverse beam, clamp-zone callout and zero-above-deck ban were already specified. I accept Structural Dynamicist ready on twin-detuned hold 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 from the detuning sweep (E70) with off-antinode 0.75 from the modal effectiveness calculation (E67), Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead ready on transverse midspan pair within girder depth with from-below service by Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), with no deck hatch, Bridge Retrofit Engineer ready on clamp with beam steel inside 2 percent and stop load fed back, and Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor ready on Medium with Multiple Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Multiple Tuned Mass Damper (MTMD), robustness from the comfort review (E48), with the instrumented Class III crowd walk-through kept as the after-build bench test.

RECORD: Decided twin 400 kg Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) pair on HSFG-clamped transverse cross-beam at midspan antinode below soffit within girder depth with 80 mm stops and crowd acceptance run; numbers that stand are 800 kg total (E13) 7.85 kN (E26) 1.31 percent TMD-only and 1.69 percent total (E72)(E76) 1.83 Hz (E14) 12.0 percent (E15) 6.20 percent effective (E17) 0.67 m/s2 versus 8.28 m/s2 (E45)(E43) 49.4 mm 80 mm 74.7 mm 124 mm (E17)(E63)(E68) 32.9 kN versus 13.1 kN plus 8.40 kN (E64)(E65)(E66); still open is only the after-build Class III crowd walk-through bench test with no owner owed in concept design.

Note on Structural Dynamicist: Vertical midspan drive and detuned robustness hold with evidence.
Note on Bridge Retrofit Engineer: Slip margin with stop load and total weight inside 2 percent hold with evidence.
Note on Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor: Medium verdict with robustness and zero-above-deck ban hold with evidence.
Note on Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead: Transverse station, below-flange zone and from-below access jointly confirm both locks.

My position is ready, because physics, loads, comfort and depiction topology all stand with no blocking objection open.
